title: Job
description: An enqueued clusterbuck job record — the payload the coordinator writes onto a capability stream and a worker consumes. This is the cross-language seam (protocols.md §2); addressing has already been resolved to a concrete `capability` before enqueue.

capability.description: Resolved supply-side capability tier, e.g. "8b-extract". Names the queue `q:<capability>`. The coordinator resolves task_class+min_ability to this before enqueue.

messages.description: OpenAI-style chat messages. Present unless `prompt` is used.

params.description: Inference parameters passed through to the model server.

model.description: Optional artifact pin: overrides the worker's configured model for this job. The eval harness relies on this to attribute a score to the artifact actually under test rather than to whatever the worker defaults to, so a worker MUST forward it to the model server.

response_format.description: Hint only; local model servers do not reliably honour structured-output flags (protocols.md §3). JSON shape is requested in the prompt and validated by the client.

urgency.description: A trajectory, not a static label (ADR 18). Carries wake rights.

escalate_after_min.description: waitable only: patience bound (not a delay). Unserved after N minutes it escalates to necessary.

privacy.description: local_only NEVER routes off-LAN, at any urgency (ADR 14).

deadline.description: Optional expiry. Enforced by a coordinator sweep that withdraws the entry if no worker has claimed it and marks the job `expired`. A worker does not check this field, so a job already claimed runs to completion — but its late result is discarded: `expired` is final and no later result overrides it. Absent means no expiry: a waitable job with neither this nor `escalate_after_min` has no terminating mechanism at all (protocols.md §1b).

result_key.description: Result-store key the worker writes the result under (write-once).

max_attempts.description: After this many attempts the job fails rather than requeues.

submitter.description: Optional caller provenance: which client submitted this job, from where, and under which logical request. IDENTIFICATION ONLY — the coordinator never dedupes, collapses, reorders or rejects on these fields. Absent on jobs from clients that predate it, so every consumer must treat it as optional.

app.description: Client application name, e.g. "nightly-importer". Opaque to clusterbuck, which never interprets or branches on it (domain-agnostic).

instance.description: Hostname of the machine the call came from — distinguishes two copies of the same app running on different nodes.

request_id.description: Client-supplied UID identifying one LOGICAL call. This is the duplicate-vs-repeat discriminator: two jobs sharing a request_id are the same call retried (a duplicate — a client retry loop), whereas two jobs with identical content but different request_ids are genuinely repeated work. Never enforced as unique; a client that reuses one is describing a retry, not violating a constraint.

submitted_at.description: The client's own clock at submission. ADVISORY ONLY — useful as a clock-skew / queue-delay signal. `created_at` (server-stamped at receipt) remains authoritative for every ordering, escalation and metering decision, and nothing in the coordinator may read this instead.

requires.description: Hard capability requirements (ADR 37): what the model must be able to DO, as opposed to how well it does it. Applied by the coordinator as a filter BEFORE ability is compared, because these are yes/no facts no 1-10 score can express — a 4k-context model and a 128k one can both honestly be 'a 6 at summarize', and routing a 60k-token document to the first silently truncates it. An artifact that does not DECLARE a required feature is excluded by name: undeclared reads as no, because an unchecked feature fails at the model server where it looks like a model bug rather than a routing one, or worse succeeds while quietly ignoring the request. Carried on the wire because the worker acts on `json_schema`.

context_tokens.description: Minimum context window, in tokens. Compared against the model's published window, not whatever a given server was started with.

json_schema.description: Requires schema-constrained output. This is also what licenses the worker to forward `params.response_format`: without the requirement, routing has not checked that the model can honour it, so it stays a dropped hint.
